blindSummary:
This country carries serious and recently deteriorating risk for trans visitors. Long considered a tolerant outlier in its region (same-sex conduct has never been criminalised), it saw a wave of violence in late 2024: social-media influencers exhorted followers to "hunt" gay and gender-nonconforming people, and dozens of assaults and beatings followed (reporting by a foreign newspaper, Oct 2024). There is no legal gender recognition and no anti-discrimination protection; police response to the hunt wave was inadequate.

For a visitor: no statutory exposure, but the 2024 hunt-down campaign makes visible gender nonconformity dangerous, especially in the country's largest city.
blindOutOfScope: The 2024 violence wave targeted perceived gay men primarily but gender-nonconforming people are the most visible targets.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying foreign-newspaper article (Oct 2024) covers the situation of LGBTQ people in this country.

UNDP report (Dec 2024) marking the tenth anniversary of a resolution of a regional human-rights body on protection against violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity - includes a country overview for this country assessing the protective legal environment, investigation/prosecution of perpetrators, access to justice, civic space, and inclusion of LGBT+ people.

A foreign government's 2023 human-rights report on this country: official assessment including the SOGI section - same-sex conduct not criminalised but societal discrimination, and significant violence against LGBT persons documented in the report period.

A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: post-electoral-crisis context (3,000 deaths, sexual violence, displacement) - general human-rights baseline with limited LGBT-specific content.

Academic article (2015, regional-studies journal) by two researchers: on violence, exclusion and resilience among people assigned male at birth who live as women (a local borrowed term designates this population) - they encounter harsher stigmatisation than other sexual/gender minorities in this country; documents violence, exclusion and community resilience.
Same article as above (canonical archive URL): the key academic source on trans-feminine people's experiences in this country.
